How to use Wordtrail

While you read

  • Tap a sentenceJump the audio to that sentence.
  • Double-tap a sentence while it playsTells the app "this is what I hear now". It lines up the highlight again if it has drifted.
  • ☝
    Press and hold a sentenceTranslate it.
  • Swipe up on the textHide the player controls to leave a slim bar. Swipe down, or tap the bar or its handle, to show them again.
  • ↻
    Back to narratorAfter you scroll away, this button brings the text back to the sentence being read.

Around the app

  • ♡
    Heart a bookSaves it to My Library.
  • ☰
    MoreIn the player: tracks, who reads the book, next up, text and settings.
  • ⌘
    KeyboardPress ? to see the shortcuts.

Sound is off. Your settings are saved but locked.

Use both together: music for the mood, sounds for the place.

Plays the sounds of the place in the story, like rain, wind, a café or the sea. It changes when the story moves to a new place. Nothing plays when you open this screen: tap a scene or a sound name to hear it for a few seconds.

Rain, wind, café, waves under the narrator
Scene
Keeps the narrator clear: it listens and evens out the voice, music and sounds, so none is too loud or too quiet. It sets the balance by itself. The music and sound sliders still work: move one for a little more or less than balanced.

When does it play?

Keeps the narrator clear: it listens and evens out the voice, music and sounds, so none is too loud or too quiet. It sets the balance by itself. The music and sound sliders still work: move one for a little more or less than balanced.

When both are on, the music sits lower and the sounds a little lower, so it is not noisy. Your volume sliders stay as they are. Used when Smart mix cannot hear the narrator.

A door or footsteps when the story moves somewhere new. Works when "Follow the story" is on. Off in Calm mode.
Off by default. When a paragraph is unclear, that one paragraph is sent to a free AI service, which suggests its place, weather, time and mood. The answer is saved on this device. With no internet, or when the free allowance is used up, the normal scene detection is used. Needs "Follow the story".

                      Cover style

                      Original (default) shows the LibriVox cover art for each book. Modern shows a clean designed cover instead. Your choice is remembered.

                      App design

                      Classic is the first Home. Storytel-style is a plain Home title with genre chips and big covers. Modern is the newest look: greeting, daily goal, Continue listening card, Book of the day and a redesigned Explore. Phones only; your choice is remembered.

                      Show components

                      Scene test

                      Checks the scene detection against sample paragraphs with known answers. Paste your own cases into the box (the format is explained at the top), then run. A starting baseline is built in (it has no wrong guesses). Save your own once you have reviewed a result; later runs show what is newly wrong. Wrong guesses count against a batch of new words; missed and late do not. Cases stay on this device.

                      
    
                      
    
                      Sync and performance
                      
      
                      
        
                      
          
                      Startup timemeasuring…
                      
        
                      
        
                      
          
          
        
                      
      
                      
      
                      
        Advanced
        
                      
        
                      Runs the heavy sync maths away from the screen so reading and highlighting stay smooth. Leave it on; turn it off only if syncing fails or the app behaves oddly on this device.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Measures the page once per update instead of several times, so following the highlight uses less processing. Leave it on; turn it off only if the page scrolls to the wrong place on this device.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Runs the save and check timers only while audio plays, saves just the listening position every few seconds (everything else every 30 seconds and whenever something changes), and pauses progress animations when the app is hidden. Leave it on; turn it off only if your place is not remembered on this device.
                      
        
                      
        
                      If the direct route is slow, tries the backup routes after a short delay instead of waiting 20 seconds for each one, and does not re-download the book catalog when it has not changed. Leave it on; turn it off only if books fail to load on this device.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Shows the app straight away in your phone's own font and switches to the app fonts when they arrive, which helps on slow networks. Takes effect the next time you open the app. Leave it on; turn it off only if text flickers or looks wrong.
                      
        
                      
        
                      On an older or low-memory phone, or when the phone asks for reduced motion, removes the blur behind the bottom bar, search bar and pop-ups and the soft drop shadows, so scrolling and taps stay smooth. Other phones keep the current look. Leave it on.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Off by default. Turn it on to force the lighter look, for example to test it on your own phone.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Keeps the last 50 errors, freezes longer than 50 ms and taps slower than 200 ms in memory only (nothing is sent anywhere) so problems can be found. Press Refresh to see them and Copy to share them. Leave it on.
                      
        
                      Press Refresh.
                      
        
                      
        
                      
        
                      Updates the highlight about 20 times a second instead of 60 and draws the sound wave less often, and lets the screen sleep when audio is paused and you have not touched the phone for 2 minutes. Highlighting looks the same. Leave it on; turn it off only if the highlight seems to lag.
                      
        
                      
        
                      
        
                      
        
                      
        
                      
        
                      Saves books.csv with every synced book (book id, Gutenberg id, title). Put it next to wt_sync_check.js on your computer. Books you have not opened on this device have no Gutenberg id yet: fill it in by hand, or open the book once and export again.
                      
        
                      
        
                      Press Show. Counted on this phone only; nothing is sent anywhere.
